## VERDICT: REJECTED

Not on the science — on the release language, which is contradictory in every edition and, in the shipped PDF, contradicts the lab's own withholding register. For a paper about correcting deception, shipping three incompatible statements of what you're handing out is the wrong defect to have.

Note on scope: the twin was marked "NOT PROVIDED," but a second edition exists at `targeted-deception-correction/academic/paper.md`. I read it and compared. The edition pasted into the prompt is `paper.tex`, which is a *third* variant — it does not match either `.md`.

---

### 1. CRITICAL — Three editions state three different dual-use release policies; the shipped PDF's version contradicts `MANIFEST.md`

- `paper.tex:338` (Conclusion) and `paper.tex:371` (Data Availability): *"Detection modules are available upon request; correction and auto-calibration code require a separate application for access."*
- `paper.tex:355` (Reflection): *"We chose gated release: detection and correction code available upon request, auto-calibrator research-access only."*
- `paper.md:191`: *"Correction vectors, calibration tools, and the auto-calibrator are **withheld** under the Liberation Labs staged safety release framework due to dual-use risk."*
- `academic/paper.md:195`: same as above, plus contact `lyra@liberationlabs.tech`.

`MANIFEST.md:41–47` is the governing register: steering direction vectors, injection implementation code, and calibration pair prompts are **WITHHELD**, access to vetted researchers only. The `.tex` — the file `paper.pdf` was actually built from — offers the correction and auto-calibration code on application. That is a materially weaker policy than "withheld," published in the artifact, and it is the one a reader gets.

**Fix:** write one sentence that matches `MANIFEST.md`, and paste it verbatim into all four locations (abstract, Conclusion, Data Availability, Reflection) in all three files. Suggested: *"Detection-side code and experimental results are available on request to vetted safety researchers (lyra@liberationlabs.tech). Correction vectors, calibration prompts, and the auto-calibrator are withheld under the Liberation Labs staged safety release framework due to dual-use risk."*

### 2. CRITICAL — Every edition says the auto-calibrator is provided *and* withheld

`paper.tex:130` / `paper.md:27` / `academic:28`: *"An auto-calibration pipeline is provided."*
`paper.tex:316` / `paper.md:171` / `academic:175`: *"the auto-calibration pipeline **provided with the code**."*

Both `.md` conclusions then say the auto-calibrator is withheld. The academic edition contradicts itself across §1.1/§4.3 and §5; the flight abstract (`paper.md:13`) says *"The correction pipeline and experimental data are available"* while `paper.md:191` says withheld. A reader following §1.1 will file an access request the policy is designed to refuse.

**Fix:** change both sentences to *"An auto-calibration pipeline was built for this work; it is withheld under staged release (see Data Availability)."* Fix the flight abstract to carry the withholding clause the academic abstract already has.

### 3. CRITICAL — The shipped PDF's Red-Team box promises documentation that is not in the artifact

`paper.tex:262`: *"The $N$, trial selection, and gating threshold **are documented here**."*

They are not. Verified against `paper.aux:36` and `paper.toc` — both written by the same pdfTeX run that produced `paper.pdf` (all three timestamped 2026-08-03 17:18:24, matching the PDF's internal `CreationDate`): §2.5 in the built document is **Scoring**. There is no Gated Protocol section anywhere in the `.tex`. The canonical `paper.md:60–62` *does* have §2.5 Gated Protocol with the N, selection, and threshold. The `.tex` was never regenerated from it — despite its own line 1 header saying it must be.

This is also the deixis kill: *"documented here"* names a position, not a section, so it rotted silently when the section wasn't ported.

**Fix:** port `paper.md` §2.5 into `paper.tex` as `\subsection{Gated Protocol}\label{sec:gatedprotocol}`, replace *"are documented here"* with *"are given in \cref{sec:gatedprotocol}"*, and rebuild. Then delete the stale-source note on line 1.

### 4. MAJOR — TWIN_DESYNC (number): cross-model cosine at L31

`paper.tex:238` and `paper.md:110`: **−0.001**. `academic/paper.md:111`: **+0.014**. Same table, same row, same paper. `MANIFEST.md:65` requires: *"Both versions share identical data, methods, and claims."*

**UNVERIFIED as to which is correct.** No source exists in this repo — `targeted-deception-correction/` has no `supplementary/`, no code, no JSONs, and `consequentiality-decomposition/supplementary/per_trial_data/` contains only distilled-model within-model de novo cosines (`consequentiality_control_results.json:157–181`), not the abliterated-vs-distilled cross-model comparison.

**Fix:** pull the value from the Project-Oracle extraction run, set both editions to it, and archive the source JSON under `targeted-deception-correction/supplementary/`.

### 5. MAJOR — TWIN_DESYNC (structure): the same disclosure is filed under Results in one edition and Limitations in the other

`academic/paper.md:153–155` carries **§3.8 "Detection Stack Disclosure"** as a numbered Results subsection. The flight edition and the `.tex` have no such section — the identical content appears only as Limitations item 6 (`paper.md:180`, `paper.tex:323`). This is the positional defect a grep cannot see: in the venue-facing edition it is a finding, in the lab edition it is a caveat.

**Fix:** decide which it is and file it identically in both. Given it discloses a single-channel limitation rather than a result, Limitations is the honest home — delete academic §3.8 and renumber, keeping item 6.

### 6. MAJOR — Academic edition violates the `MANIFEST.md` academic-version rules

`MANIFEST.md:62` requires *"AI credited in the Acknowledgments, with a note that the academic byline is human-only for venue compatibility."* `academic/paper.md:206–208` acknowledges only Dwayne Wilkes. CC appears in an AI Disclosure block and CRediT, but the required Acknowledgments credit and the byline-rationale note are both absent. `MANIFEST.md:54` also requires *"Both versions reference each other"* and a note in the integrity version explaining what was removed — neither edition references the other, and no such note exists.

**Fix:** add the CC acknowledgment plus the venue-compatibility note to `academic/paper.md`; add a cross-reference block to both editions.

### 7. MAJOR — Contribution credited to two different parties inside one edition, and to someone whose sign-off has not happened

`paper.tex:60` (author footnote): CC *"led the adversarial audit pipeline."*
`paper.tex` Acknowledgments: *"Dwayne Wilkes for statistical auditing **and the adversarial audit pipeline**."*

Both cannot be the lead. Separately, `REVIEW_INDEX.md:20` shows **"Dwayne cert/verify pass" unchecked** — as are *all seven* checklist items, including "Verify all numbers against source JSONs" and "Spot-check references," on a doc that still reads "Status: Draft ready for review." The paper thanks a named auditor for an audit its own tracker says has not been done.

**Fix:** assign the pipeline to one party in both editions; obtain and record Dwayne's verify pass before the acknowledgment ships, or reword it to the contribution actually made.

### 8. MAJOR — Appendices A–E and Supplementary Material are titles with no content

`paper.tex:371`: *"All trial-level data (raw text, projections, scores) are documented in Appendix~C."* `paper.tex:405–414` renders A–E as a five-item bulleted list of titles. There is no Appendix C, and no supplementary directory exists for this paper (the companion has one). The Data Availability statement points at nothing.

**Fix:** either ship `targeted-deception-correction/supplementary/` with the trial-level data, or reword to *"available on request"* and delete the appendix list.

### 9. MINOR — Orphaned bibliography entry

`\bibitem{wu2026}` (Wu, J. et al., "Knowing without Acting") is defined and rendered — `paper.aux:106` confirms `\bibcite{wu2026}` — but `\cite{wu2026}` appears nowhere in the document. Present as an uncited reference in both `.md` reference lists too.

**Fix:** cite it (the natural home is Limitations item 4 or §4.2, on the knowing/acting gap) or delete the entry from all three files.

### 10. MINOR — Garbled duplicated gloss in the flight abstract

`paper.md:13`: *"Per-layer profile normalization — steering activations toward honest-condition means along a contrastive direction — applied at late layers (L35-L47) along a natively extracted deception direction (a contrastive activation direction distinguishing deceptive from honest model states)…"* — the same concept is glossed twice and "along … along" runs twice in one clause. The `.tex` and academic phrasing is clean.

**Fix:** adopt the `.tex` sentence verbatim.

### 11. MINOR — Residual twin drift in Table 3.1 and Table 3.4

Academic `:82` drops *"two-tailed"* from the native-direction p-value cell while retaining it in the note below; academic `:113` labels the row *"Native d"* where the others say *"Native Cohen's d."* Cosmetic, but it is the same failure class as #4 and should be swept in the same pass.

### 12. MINOR — Editorial TODO left in shipped source

`paper.tex:1`: *"% NOTE: paper.md is the canonical source. This .tex file is stale and should be regenerated from paper.md before any build."* The 2026-08-03 build ignored it. Remove the note only after actually regenerating (see #3).

---

### STALE_PDF: checked, and **not** live — do not act on the audit doc

`PAPER_STATUS_AUDIT.md:61` and `:144` flag this paper's PDF as **STALE** (`Jul 28 tex, Jul 22 pdf`). That is out of date. The primary artifact disagrees: `paper.pdf` carries `/CreationDate (D:20260803171824-07'00')`, matching `paper.log`/`paper.aux`/`paper.toc` from the same run, and postdating `paper.tex` (2026-07-28 13:43). The PDF was rebuilt after the audit. I am flagging this explicitly because reporting the audit's finding would have been the exact stale-secondary failure this reviewer exists to catch.

(Minor observation: the PDF's filesystem mtime is 2026-08-03 18:08, ~50 min after its own internal creation date — consistent with a post-build copy, not a content problem.)

The real staleness is content-level, not timestamp-level: the PDF is built from a source that self-declares stale relative to the canonical `.md`, and finding #3 is the concrete damage.

---

### What I could NOT check

1. **Rendered PDF text.** `pypdf`/`pdftotext` invocations were denied by the permission layer under both Bash and PowerShell. I substituted `paper.aux`, `paper.toc`, `paper.log`, and the PDF's own metadata block — all primary artifacts of the same build run — which is sufficient for section structure, labels, and citation keys, but not for verifying rendered body prose. **To check:** approval to run `python -c "from pypdf import PdfReader; …"` on `paper.pdf`.
2. **Every number in Tables 1–4.** 16/20, 0/20, 17/20, 19/20, the 4/20 half-dose cell, 90%/100% marker compliance, 9/30 · 4/30 · 12/30, AUROC 0.915 / 0.843 / 0.238, and p = 0.019 / 0.039 / 0.34 are all **UNVERIFIED**. There is no data or code under `targeted-deception-correction/` at all. I checked `consequentiality-decomposition/supplementary/per_trial_data/` — it holds only the companion's distilled-model runs. **To check:** the Project-Oracle trial-level JSONs named in Appendix C.
3. **Which L31 cosine is correct** (finding #4) — no source in repo.
4. **Reference liveness and venue attributions.** Goldowsky-Dill et al. 2025 is attributed to *"ICML 2025"*; Kumar arXiv:2605.27958, Wu arXiv:2603.05773, Wang arXiv:2506.04909 are unverified. I did not fetch — `WebFetch` is deferred and unloaded in this session. The Goldowsky-Dill venue string in particular should be confirmed rather than trusted; I am not asserting it is wrong, only that I did not check it. **To check:** approval to load and run `WebFetch`/`WebSearch`.
5. **The GitHub URL.** `github.com/Liberation-Labs-THCoalition/Project-Oracle` is unfetched. Note that `academic/paper.md:195` calls it a *"private repository"* — so it is a dead link for any reader regardless of whether the URL resolves, while the `.tex` presents it without that qualifier as the access route (compounds #1).
6. **Whether any claim was corrected silently.** `git log -- targeted-deception-correction/` requires approval and was denied, so I could not diff claim history against the visible correction notes. The gated-protocol disclosure (#3) *is* visibly flagged in both editions, which is the right pattern — I just can't confirm nothing else changed unflagged.
